name: Avatar
introduction: Uses local Waves fallbacks for rounded organization avatars and Glyphs for users.

properties.name: name
properties.description: User name for initials and alt text.

properties.name: shape
properties.description: Shape variant of the avatar. 'circle' (default) stays fully round. 'rounded' uses the element radius token so it matches UI corner rounding and can be set globally via theme. 'square' has no radius. Status dot positioning adapts automatically: 4-o'clock on circle, bottom-right corner on rounded/square. Default: 'circle'.

properties.name: src
properties.description: Primary image source URL.

properties.name: alt
properties.description: Alt text (falls back to name).

properties.name: size
properties.description: Avatar size. Use a named size ('xsm' 20px, 'sm' 24px, 'md' 36px, 'lg' 48px, 'xl' 128px) or a numeric pixel value. Avatar shares Icon's abbreviated scale, but its tiers are larger because avatars align with media rather than glyphs. Inside an AvatarGroup the group's size wins and this prop is ignored. Default: 'md'.

practices.description: Pick a size that matches the context: xsm or sm for inline mentions, md or lg for lists and cards, xl for profile headers.
Use Avatar for logos, product images, or anything that isn't a person or team. Use an image or icon instead.

name: Badge
introduction: Displays a count or enumerated state.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Badge text content. A badge is one line, so a label wider than the space available is cut with an ellipsis rather than escaping its container; a string or number label is also set as the badge's title so the full text stays reachable on hover.

properties.name: icon
properties.description: Optional leading icon.

properties.name: variant
properties.description: Visual style variant. Semantic variants (neutral, info, success, warning, error) use solid backgrounds. Non-semantic color variants use tinted backgrounds with colored text for categorization and tagging. Default: 'neutral'.

practices.description: Every status badge steals attention. Only badge states where the user needs to notice or act: errors, warnings, items requiring follow-up. If no action is needed, plain text is fine.
Use success, warning, and error variants only for system status that demands attention: "Failed", "Degraded", "Action Required". These have bold solid backgrounds designed to stand out.
Use color variants (blue, purple, teal, etc.) for category tags that group or classify items: team names, content types, priority levels.
Keep labels to one or two words. If you need more detail, put it in surrounding text instead of the badge.
Add an icon when it helps identify the badge type quickly, but always include a text label alongside it.

Apply a "success" badge to every healthy/active/normal item. If all rows show green "Active" badges, none stand out; the badge adds noise, not information. Show only the states that need user attention (errors, warnings, pending actions).
Use badges for metadata. Durations ("6h window"), counts ("12 trigger types"), dates, and descriptions are not statuses or categories; use description text (Text with type="supporting") instead.
Use semantic status variants (success, warning, error, info) for categories or informational content. These are visually loud and should only indicate system state.

Repeat the same badge in every row of a table or list. If the same value appears in most rows, it's not adding information; use plain text for common states and reserve badges for the exceptional ones.
Make badges clickable; they are read-only indicators. Use a button or link if the user needs to take action.

name: Button
introduction: Gives onClick automatic asynchronous loading and duplicate-click prevention.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Accessible label. Rendered as visible text by default; used as aria-label when isIconOnly is true.

properties.name: variant
properties.description: Visual style variant. Default: 'secondary'.

properties.name: size
properties.description: Size variant. Default: 'md'.

properties.name: type
properties.description: HTML button type attribute. Default: 'button'.

properties.name: name
properties.description: HTML name attribute for form submission.

properties.name: value
properties.description: HTML value attribute for form submission.

properties.name: form
properties.description: Associates the button with a form element by ID.

properties.name: icon
properties.description: Icon element rendered before the label text. An Astryx Icon with no explicit size defaults to sm for sm/md buttons and md for lg buttons.

properties.name: endContent
properties.description: Trailing icon or badge rendered after the label. Ignored when isIconOnly is true. Color is inherited from the button variant.

properties.name: tooltip
properties.description: Tooltip text shown on hover.

properties.name: width
properties.description: Width of the button. Numbers are treated as pixels, strings are used as-is (e.g., '100%' for a full-width button). By default the button sizes to its content.

properties.name: isDisabled
properties.description: Disables the button. When a tooltip is present, uses aria-disabled instead of native disabled so the button stays focusable. Default: false.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: The disabled prop.

properties.name: href
properties.description: When provided, renders the button as a link element (<a> or custom link component). The destination follows the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop.

properties.name: onClick
properties.description: Standard click handler (passed through from ButtonHTMLAttributes).

practices.description: Write labels that describe the action ("Save changes", "Delete account", "Send invite"), not vague labels like "OK" or "Click here".
Show a loading state for actions that take time, like saving or submitting, so the user knows it is working.
Always provide a label for icon-only buttons so screen readers can announce what the button does. Add a tooltip for sighted users.
Place more than one primary button in the same view; this dilutes the visual hierarchy.
Use the destructive variant without a confirmation step for irreversible actions like deleting data.
Use a button for navigation. If it only takes the user to another page, use a link instead. Buttons are for actions like saving, deleting, or submitting.

name: ButtonGroup
introduction: Groups related flat action buttons.

properties.name: children
properties.description: Button or IconButton children.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Accessible label for the group (aria-label).

properties.name: orientation
properties.description: Layout direction of the button group. Default: 'horizontal'.

properties.name: size
properties.description: Default size for buttons in the group. Individual buttons can override. Default: 'md'.

properties.name: isDisabled
properties.description: Whether all buttons in the group are disabled. Default: false.

practices.description: Group buttons that perform related actions on the same object, like copy, cut, paste on selected text.
Use the same variant for all buttons in a group so they look like a single connected unit.
Keep groups small (2–4 buttons). For more actions, use a Toolbar or DropdownMenu instead.
Don't mix wildly different actions. A Save button next to a Delete button in the same group is confusing.
Don't use ButtonGroup for navigation. Use SegmentedControl or TabList for switching between views.
Don't nest ButtonGroups. If you need multiple groups, place them side by side with a gap.
Name the group for what its buttons act on. The label is the group's accessible name and a screen reader reads it before each member.

Keep the group a single Tab stop. Arrow keys move between members along the orientation, Home/End jump to the ends, and disabled members are skipped. This is the WAI-ARIA APG roving tabindex technique: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_roving_tabindex

Don't disable the group to show that an action is in flight. A disabled member drops focus, so a keyboard user loses their place; leave the group enabled and show progress on the button that started the work.

name: CheckboxInput
introduction: Edits a boolean or indeterminate field.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Label text for the checkbox (always rendered for accessibility).

properties.name: description
properties.description: Description text displayed below the label.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Includes the themed control's value under this form submission name.

properties.name: required
properties.description: Requires a value before native form submission.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: Prevents interaction and excludes the field from submission.

properties.name: readOnly
properties.description: Retains submitted values while preventing editing where supported.

properties.name: isRequired
properties.description: Whether the checkbox is required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional. Default: false.

properties.name: isDisabled
properties.description: Whether the checkbox is disabled. Default: false.

properties.name: width
properties.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

properties.name: value
properties.description: Whether the checkbox is checked, unchecked, or indeterminate.

properties.name: checked
properties.description: The checked prop.

properties.name: defaultChecked
properties.description: The defaultChecked prop.

properties.name: onChange
properties.description: Callback fired when the checkbox state changes.

properties.name: isReadOnly
properties.description: Whether the checkbox is read-only. Displays the current state at full opacity but prevents interaction. Unlike `isDisabled`, read-only checkboxes are not visually dimmed. Default: false.

properties.name: htmlName
properties.description: The HTML name attribute for the underlying checkbox input, useful for form submissions (submits "on" when checked). Default: props.htmlName.

properties.name: size
properties.description: The size of the checkbox. sm for compact layouts, md for default. Default: 'md'.

practices.description: Add a description for choices that need extra context, like explaining what "Share usage data" actually shares.
Use the indeterminate state for "select all" checkboxes when only some items in a group are selected.
Use a checkbox for mutually exclusive choices; use RadioList when only one option can be selected.
Use a checkbox for actions that take effect immediately; use a toggle switch or button instead.

name: CodeBlock
introduction: Displays source code using standard copy and highlighting behavior.

properties.name: code
properties.description: The code string to display.

properties.name: language
properties.description: Language for syntax highlighting. Use "plaintext" to disable. Default: 'plaintext'.

properties.name: title
properties.description: Filename or label shown in the header bar.

properties.name: isWrapped
properties.description: Wrap long lines instead of enabling horizontal scroll. Default: false.

practices.description: Set the language prop to match the code content so syntax highlighting is accurate. Use "plaintext" when the language is unknown.
Add a title when the code represents a file. It gives readers context and appears in the header bar alongside the copy button.
Use Code for short inline references like function names or CLI flags, and CodeBlock for standalone multi-line snippets.
Enable line numbers on short snippets (under 5 lines) where they add clutter without helping navigation.

name: Collapsible
introduction: Shows or hides content using controlled or initially open state.

properties.name: children
properties.description: Content that collapses and expands.

properties.name: trigger
properties.description: Content shown in the trigger area (always visible).

properties.name: defaultIsOpen
properties.description: Default open state (uncontrolled). Default: true.

properties.name: isOpen
properties.description: Controlled open state.

properties.name: isDisabled
properties.description: Disable the item so its trigger can't be toggled (dimmed, aria-disabled, and out of the tab order). Doesn't collapse an already-open item. Default: false.

properties.name: onOpenChange
properties.description: Callback invoked when the open state changes.

practices.description: Use hasDividers on CollapsibleGroup for FAQ-style lists: built-in row hairlines with themed border tokens, no hand-rolled borders.
Wrap each Collapsible in an Card for visual separation in accordion layouts, or use CollapsibleGroup's hasDividers for flat lists; don't combine both.
Use CollapsibleGroup with type="single" for settings or FAQ pages where only one section should be open at a time.
Use type="multiple" when users need to compare content across sections, like feature lists or pricing tiers.
Start sections open (defaultIsOpen) when the content is likely needed on first view; don't make users click to see essential info.
Hide critical or required content behind a collapsible; users may not discover it.
Nest collapsibles more than two levels deep; it makes content hard to find and navigate.
Use a collapsible for a single short paragraph; just show the text directly instead.

name: DateInput
introduction: Selects a constrained date with standard month and week presentation.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Label text.

properties.name: description
properties.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Includes the themed control's value under this form submission name.

properties.name: required
properties.description: Requires a value before native form submission.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: Prevents interaction and excludes the field from submission.

properties.name: readOnly
properties.description: Retains submitted values while preventing editing where supported.

properties.name: isRequired
properties.description: Mark the field as required. Default: false.

properties.name: isDisabled
properties.description: Disable the input and calendar. Default: false.

properties.name: width
properties.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

properties.name: value
properties.description: Selected date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

properties.name: defaultValue
properties.description: The defaultValue prop.

properties.name: onChange
properties.description: Callback invoked when the selected date changes.

properties.name: min
properties.description: Minimum selectable date (YYYY-MM-DD).

properties.name: max
properties.description: Maximum selectable date (YYYY-MM-DD).

properties.name: dateConstraints
properties.description: Additional constraints applied to the themed calendar picker.

properties.name: placeholder
properties.description: Placeholder text shown in the text input. Default: 'Select a date'.

properties.name: hasClear
properties.description: Shows a clear (×) button when a date value is set. Clicking it clears the value and returns focus to the input. Default: false.

properties.name: size
properties.description: Size of the input control. Default: 'md'.

practices.description: Provide clear labels and descriptions so users understand what date is expected.
Use min, max, and dateConstraints to restrict selectable dates to valid ranges.
Use hasClear when the date is optional so the user can reset it.
Use DateInput inside InputGroup when adding a short static prefix or suffix, such as a due-date hint.
Use a DateInput for free-form text that does not represent a calendar date.
Hide the label without surrounding context that makes the field purpose obvious.
Rely on the calendar alone; the text input lets users type dates directly, which is faster for known dates.

name: Dialog
introduction: Displays an accessible modal with an explicit purpose and controlled visibility.

properties.name: children
properties.description: Dialog content.

properties.name: aria-label
properties.description: The aria-label prop.

properties.name: isOpen
properties.description: Whether the dialog is open.

properties.name: onOpenChange
properties.description: Callback when dialog visibility changes.

properties.name: purpose
properties.description: Controls dismissal behavior: required disables Escape and backdrop click; form disables backdrop click after interaction; info allows both. Default: 'info'.

practices.description: Choose the right purpose: info for dismissable content, form to prevent accidental backdrop dismissal, required when the user must respond.
Include a clear title in the header so users immediately understand what the dialog is asking.
Use purpose="form" for dialogs with inputs so the user can't accidentally lose data by clicking the backdrop.
Keep dialogs focused on a single task; if the content grows beyond what fits, consider a full page instead.
Use a dialog for simple messages that could be shown inline or as a toast notification.
Nest dialogs inside other dialogs; restructure the flow into steps within a single dialog instead.

name: Divider
introduction: Separates View content with an optional label and configurable line presentation.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Optional label centered on the divider.

properties.name: variant
properties.description: Visual weight of the divider line. Default: 'subtle'.

properties.name: orientation
properties.description: Orientation of the divider. Default: 'horizontal'.

properties.name: isFullBleed
properties.description: Extend the divider to container edges with negative margins. Default: false.

practices.description: Use subtle dividers between related content sections and strong dividers for high-contrast boundaries.
Add a label to the divider when sections need a visible category heading.
Overuse dividers; rely on spacing and layout to separate content when possible.

name: DropdownMenu
introduction: Opens an action menu using standard adaptive presentation and placement.

properties.name: button
properties.type: { label: string; variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "destructive"; size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg"; isDisabled?: boolean; }
properties.description: Props for the trigger button (Button props except onClick). Default: { label: 'Menu', variant: 'secondary', size: 'md', isDisabled: false }.

properties.name: items
properties.description: Array of menu entries. Each entry is one of: an action item `{label, onClick?, icon?, description?, endContent?, isDisabled?, variant?, hasCloseOnSelect?, id?}` (variant `"destructive"` renders it in the error color; `endContent` holds trailing content such as a keyboard-shortcut hint; `id` is the row's stable React key, needed only when the array reorders or filters), a divider `{type: "divider"}`, or a section `{type: "section", title?, id?, items: [...action items]}`.

properties.name: isMenuOpen
properties.description: Controlled open state for the menu. Mounting with true renders the menu open without moving focus into it; focus moves to the first item only when the menu opens after mount.

properties.name: onOpenChange
properties.description: Callback fired when the open state changes.

practices.description: Keep menu items concise and action-oriented so users can scan options quickly.
Use sections and dividers to group related actions when the menu has many items.
For a hierarchy that cannot fit as adjacent flyouts on a compact touch surface, a product may explicitly use a drill-in interaction with a Back action.
When the content is no longer a short list of immediate actions, reevaluate the interaction and choose a component that matches the actual task; content traits alone do not determine the component.
Use a DropdownMenu for navigation; use a navigation component instead.
Place more than 10–12 items in a single menu without grouping them into sections.

name: EmptyState
introduction: Describes an empty View region without custom decorative slots.

properties.name: title
properties.description: Primary message rendered as an <h3> heading inside the empty state.

properties.name: isCompact
properties.description: Enables the compact variant with reduced spacing for constrained content areas. Default: false.

practices.description: Include a clear title and a call-to-action button so users know how to proceed.
Use the compact variant inside cards or sidebars where space is limited.
Leave an empty state without guidance; always explain what happened and what the user can do next.
Use a generic message like "No data"; be specific about what is empty and why.
Use an EmptyState for error messages that require immediate action; use a Banner instead.

name: FileInput
introduction: Selects files with explicit upload constraints; uploading remains a Solution operation.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Accessible label for the file input.

properties.name: description
properties.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Includes the themed control's value under this form submission name.

properties.name: required
properties.description: Requires a value before native form submission.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: Prevents interaction and excludes the field from submission.

properties.name: readOnly
properties.description: Retains submitted values while preventing editing where supported.

properties.name: isRequired
properties.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and adds a screen-reader-only "Required" description to the trigger (assistive tech does not reliably announce aria-required on the trigger). Mutually exclusive with isOptional. Default: false.

properties.name: isDisabled
properties.description: Disables the input, preventing interaction and dimming the element. Default: false.

properties.name: width
properties.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

properties.name: value
properties.description: Currently selected file(s). Controlled component.

properties.name: onChange
properties.description: Callback fired when files are selected or removed.

properties.name: accept
properties.description: Accepted file types. Uses the HTML accept attribute format (e.g. "image/*", ".pdf,.doc").

properties.name: isMultiple
properties.description: Whether multiple files can be selected. When true, value and onChange use File[] instead of File. Default: false.

properties.name: multiple
properties.description: The multiple prop.

properties.name: maxSize
properties.description: Maximum file size in bytes. Files exceeding this are rejected with an error status.

properties.name: maxFiles
properties.description: Maximum number of files (only applies when isMultiple is true).

properties.name: placeholder
properties.description: Placeholder text shown when no file is selected. Default: (multiple ? 'Choose files' : 'Choose file').

properties.name: mode
properties.description: Visual mode. 'input' is a compact inline style; 'dropzone' is a larger area with drag-and-drop support. Default: 'input'.

practices.description: Always specify an accept prop to guide users toward valid file types.
Use maxSize and maxFiles to prevent oversized uploads; the component handles validation and error display automatically.
Add a description to communicate constraints like file size limits or accepted formats.
Don't use FileInput for directory or folder uploads; that is not supported in v1.
Don't avoid dropzone mode unless space is constrained; drag-and-drop is the expected interaction for file uploads.

name: Grid
introduction: Arranges View content into a fixed number of columns.

properties.name: children
properties.description: Grid content.

properties.name: columns
properties.description: Column configuration. Use a number for fixed columns (e.g. `columns={3}`). Use an object for responsive columns: `minWidth` sets the minimum column width in px, `repeat` controls track behavior (`"fill"` preserves empty tracks for consistent widths, `"fit"` collapses empty tracks so items stretch; defaults to `"fill"`), and `max` caps the maximum number of columns. Default: 1.

properties.name: gap
properties.description: Spacing between all items. Default: 3.

practices.description: Use responsive columns for layouts that should adapt to screen size: `columns={{minWidth: 280}}`.
Cap the column count with `max` to prevent rows from getting too wide on large screens.
Write manual CSS grid; Grid handles spacing and responsive behavior for you.
Use `HStack` with wrapping for grids; use Grid instead.

name: Heading
introduction: Displays a semantic View heading without a separate visual-level override.

properties.name: children
properties.description: Heading content.

properties.name: level
properties.description: Heading level. Determines the semantic HTML element (h1-h6) and the visual styling from the theme (unless `type` is set). Default: 2.

practices.description: Enable hasTabularNumbers for columns of numeric data so digits align vertically across rows.
Skip heading levels in the document outline; go h1 then h2 then h3, never h1 then h3.

Use raw HTML tags like

,

–

, or for text; Text and Heading apply the correct theme tokens automatically.
Use Text for headings; use Heading with a `level` prop (1–6) for section titles and headings.

name: Icon
introduction: Renders a registered Lucide icon at the requested Astryx size.

properties.name: icon
properties.description: Semantic icon name or SVG component. Valid semantic names: close, chevronDown, chevronLeft, chevronRight, chevronsLeft, chevronsRight, check, success, error, warning, info, calendar, clock, externalLink, menu, moreHorizontal, search, arrowUp, arrowDown, arrowsUpDown, funnel, eyeSlash, viewColumns, copy, checkDouble, wrench, stop, microphone. For any icon not in this list, pass an SVG component directly (e.g. import from lucide-react or @heroicons/react). Note: this prop is called `icon`, not `name`.

properties.name: size
properties.description: Icon size. An explicit value wins. When omitted, Icon uses the nearest default supplied by an owning Astryx component for its icon slot, then falls back to md when no contextual default exists.

practices.description: Use semantic icon names when available; they adapt to theme changes automatically.

Override icons through the theme, not globally: defineTheme({icons: {close: <XMarkIcon />}}) scopes the swap to the active <Theme>, and extends shallow-merges it into derived themes. registerIcons() mutates a process-wide registry and warns in dev, so keep it for app bootstrap rather than making it a library's theming seam.
Be mindful of context; decorative icons in compact components can distract rather than help.
Use icons as the sole means of conveying meaning; always provide a text alternative.
Resize icons with arbitrary pixel values; use the provided size props.
Mix icon styles (e.g. outline and filled) within the same context.
Pass a `name` prop; Icon uses `icon` (not `name`) to specify which icon to render.

name: IconButton
introduction: Runs a labeled icon action with automatic async feedback.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Accessible label. Used as aria-label (not rendered as visible text).

properties.name: icon
properties.description: Icon element rendered inside the button. An Astryx Icon with no explicit size defaults to sm for sm/md buttons and md for lg buttons.

properties.name: variant
properties.description: Visual style variant. Default: 'secondary'.

properties.name: size
properties.description: Size variant. Default: 'md'.

properties.name: tooltip
properties.description: Tooltip text shown on hover.

properties.name: isDisabled
properties.description: Disables the button. Default: false.

properties.name: onClick
properties.description: Standard click handler.

practices.description: Make the aria-label specific: a trash icon labeled "Delete conversation" is clearer than just "Delete" for screen readers.
Add a tooltip: even a gear icon can mean Settings, Preferences, or Configure.
Use ghost in toolbars and dense areas to reduce visual clutter.
Use IconButton if the action isn't obvious from the icon alone; use Button with text.
Skip the tooltip; label only reaches screen readers, sighted users need the hover hint.

name: Link
introduction: Displays a destination without granting a View top-level browser navigation.

properties.name: to
properties.description: The to prop.

properties.name: children
properties.description: Link content

practices.description: Write descriptive, concise link text that clearly communicates the destination.
Use Link for actions that do not navigate; use a Button instead.
Use generic text like "click here" or "read more"; describe the destination.

name: MetadataList
introduction: Lists labeled values without configurable truncation or label geometry.

properties.name: children
properties.description: Metadata items (MetadataListItem components).

properties.name: columns
properties.description: Column layout mode. Default: 'single'.

properties.name: title
properties.description: Optional title or heading above the list.

practices.description: Use for extensive form input; use a form layout instead.
Use for data that doesn't have a clear key-value structure.

name: MoreMenu
introduction: Opens additional actions without exposing popup geometry or presentation modes.

properties.name: items
properties.description: Menu items: data array of actions, dividers, and sections. Same type as DropdownMenu items prop.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Accessible label for the trigger button (aria-label) and tooltip text. Default: 'More options'.

properties.name: icon
properties.description: Override the default three-dot icon. Accepts any ReactNode.

properties.name: isDisabled
properties.description: Whether the menu trigger is disabled. Default: false.

properties.name: onOpenChange
properties.description: Callback fired when the menu opens or closes.

practices.description: Use for overflow or secondary actions; keep primary actions visible outside the menu.
Use dividers or sections to group related actions when the menu has many items.
Hide primary actions inside a MoreMenu; they should be directly visible.

name: MultiSelector
introduction: Selects multiple values using standard option and selected-value rendering.

properties.name: label
properties.description: Label text for accessibility.

properties.name: description
properties.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

properties.name: name
properties.description: Includes the themed control's value under this form submission name.

properties.name: required
properties.description: Requires a value before native form submission.

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: Prevents interaction and excludes the field from submission.

properties.name: readOnly
properties.description: Retains submitted values while preventing editing where supported.

properties.name: isRequired
properties.description: Marks the field as required. Default: false.

properties.name: isDisabled
properties.description: Disables the selector. Default: false.

properties.name: width
properties.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

properties.name: options
properties.description: Array of items: strings, objects with value/label/icon/disabled, dividers, or sections.

properties.name: value
properties.description: Currently selected values.

properties.name: defaultValue
properties.description: The defaultValue prop.

properties.name: onChange
properties.description: Callback fired when the selection changes.

properties.name: placeholder
properties.description: Placeholder text shown when no value is selected. Default: 'Select...'.

properties.name: size
properties.description: Size variant for the selector. Default: 'md'.

properties.name: hasSelectAll
properties.description: Whether to show a select-all checkbox. Default: false.

properties.name: hasSearch
properties.description: Whether to show a search input for filtering options. As the user types, the match count (or "No results found") is announced to screen readers via a polite live region. The search field has built-in affordances: a leading magnifier icon and, once a query is typed, a trailing clear (✕) button that resets the query and returns focus to the input. Default: false.

properties.name: isReadOnly
properties.description: Makes the selector read-only: the selected values stay visible, focusable, and included in form submission, and retain their combobox identity with aria-readonly. The selection surface, clear action, and disclosure indicator are removed. Unlike isDisabled, the control is not dimmed. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set. Default: false.

properties.name: htmlName
properties.description: The HTML name attribute for form submissions. Renders one hidden input per selected value, like a native multi-select. Default: props.htmlName.

properties.name: hasClear
properties.description: Shows a clear button when values are selected. Default: false.

practices.description: Use for a moderate, finite set of options where multiple choices are needed.
Enable search filtering when the list exceeds ~15 options.
Enable select-all when most users will want all or nearly all options selected.
Use inside InputGroup only when the control needs a short prefix or suffix addon as part of one decorated input surface; prefer count or labels trigger display so the group stays single-line.
Use for single-value selection; use Selector instead.
Show more than ~20 options without enabling search.

Default: 'date_time'.

practices.description: Use the auto format in feeds and lists so recent items show "2 hours ago" and older items show the full date automatically.
Keep formatting consistent within the same list or table; mixing relative and absolute timestamps in the same column confuses scanning.
Label every entry once a tooltip shows more than one zone; a bare abbreviation is not always recognizable (Tokyo renders as "GMT+9", not "JST").
Don't display raw Unix timestamps or ISO strings to users; always pass them through Timestamp to get a human-readable format.
Avoid system_date or system_time formats in user-facing UI; they are meant for developer tools, logs, and machine-readable contexts.
Don't disable the hover card on relative timestamps; users expect to hover for the full date when they see "3 hours ago".
Don't stack many zones into one card; it is capped at 300px wide and long labelled lines wrap. Two or three entries read well.

Don't pass a fixed-offset abbreviation like "EST" as timezoneID; it is a valid identifier but never observes daylight saving, so it reads an hour wrong for half the year. Use the region id, "America/New_York".
